rv.q: This bizarre comedy grew on me; it keeps gathering in lunatic intensity until you surrender to its madcap charms.
The only hope of salvation for Moritz von Stuelpnagel's production is for the five actors to go at this muddle with terrific energy and manic conviction and this, to their credit, they do.
The show as a whole, though, lands somewhere between a smart, bold, insightful sketch and a fully developed play.
Askins, while preaching an enlightened humanism, uses the same bludgeoning tactics as his opponents.
Hand on heart, it's hard to recommend.
But bright spots and a good cast don’t save the whole, a flimsy sketch of an idea promoted far, far beyond its means.
Hand to God turns out to be just as smug, dull and unimaginative in its portrayal of these joke Americans, these hilarious hick Bible-bashers, as any patronising and sneering BBC documentary.
I didn't laugh once. In fact I sank further and further down into my seat and prayed for the hand of God to deliver me from it – but He couldn't hear me above the surrounding din.
Once the dizzying exposition is in place, Hand to God spirals towards blissful hysteria.
So let's come out, at least, on the show itself, the funniest and filthiest puppet glove punch-up I've ever seen.

There is no doubting this play is base, vulgar and utterly outrageous, but when the puppetry makes Avenue Q look like a nice show to take your grandma, then we're happy to switch gear for some laugh-out-loud silliness. ...perhaps most shocking of all is that beneath the eye-wateringly explicit surface of Robert Askins' provocative farce, which began life Off-Off-Broadway in 2011, lies a sentiment that makes this one of the cuddlier shows on the West End...s. Askins' obsessive puerility won't be to everyone's taste...

The play here, as on Broadway, may wear out its somewhat self-consciously in-your-face welcome, but the sweet-faced Mr. Melling and his authentically accented colleagues do its gallows comedy and its darkness proud.
It's violent, blasphemous, obscene, puerile and sweaty. Oh, and it's absolutely hilarious.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this vulgar puppet comedy, with some finding it hilariously outrageous while others dismiss it as crude and pointless. The shocking puppet sex scene and Melling's performance draw praise, but many question the thin plot.
